title: Savanna's Act
official_summary:
Savanna's Act

This bill directs the Department of Justice (DOJ) to review, revise, and develop law enforcement and justice protocols to address missing or murdered Native Americans.

The bill requires DOJ to

  • provide training to law enforcement agencies on how to record tribal enrollment for victims in federal databases;
  • develop and implement a strategy to educate the public on the National Missing and Unidentified Persons System;
  • conduct specific outreach to tribes, tribal organizations, and urban Indian organizations regarding the ability to publicly enter information through the National Missing and Unidentified Persons System or other non-law enforcement sensitive portal;
  • develop regionally appropriate guidelines for response to cases of missing or murdered Native Americans;
  • provide training and technical assistance to tribes and law enforcement agencies for implementation of the developed guidelines; and
  • report statistics on missing or murdered Native Americans.

Tribes may submit their own guidelines to DOJ that respond to cases of missing or murdered Native Americans.

Additionally, the bill authorizes DOJ to provide grants for the purposes of (1) developing and implementing policies and protocols for law enforcement regarding cases of missing or murdered Native Americans, and (2) compiling and annually reporting data relating to missing or murdered Native Americans.

Federal law enforcement agencies must modify their guidelines to incorporate the guidelines developed by DOJ.

Finally, the Federal Bureau of Investigation must include gender in its annual statistics on missing and unidentified persons published on its website.

summary.headline: Savanna's Act directs the Justice Department to create protocols, training, and reporting to address missing or murdered Native Americans.
summary.what_it_does: The law requires the Department of Justice to review and develop law enforcement guidelines for cases of missing or murdered Native Americans, with guidelines that can be tailored by region. It requires training on recording tribal enrollment for victims in federal databases and public outreach about the National Missing and Unidentified Persons System. It also authorizes grants and requires federal agencies to update their own procedures to match DOJ's guidelines, and the FBI must include gender in its annual missing persons statistics. Tribes may submit their own response guidelines to DOJ.

who_it_affects.group: Native American tribes and tribal organizations
who_it_affects.how: They receive outreach, training, and technical assistance, and they may submit their own response guidelines to the Justice Department.
They are included in federal outreach about how to publicly enter information into the National Missing and Unidentified Persons System.

who_it_affects.group: Law enforcement agencies, including federal agencies
who_it_affects.how: They must receive training on recording tribal enrollment and must update their procedures to incorporate the Justice Department's guidelines.

who_it_affects.group: Families of missing or murdered Native Americans
who_it_affects.how: Their cases are to be handled under new federal guidelines, and data on these cases must be collected and reported.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on October 10, 2020, and its requirements are carried out over time by the Justice Department and the FBI; the summary does not give specific deadlines.
